miniProject.title: Tiny decoder with an independent oracle
miniProject.brief: Build a configurable decoder-only model from tensor operations in the same repository, and prove it correct without trusting a training curve: public snapshot tests for each component, a slow per-head reference for attention, and intervention tests for causality.
steps: Implement linear, embedding, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, softmax and scaled dot-product attention from tensor operations, and pass the matching CS336 tests in `tests/test_model.py` and `tests/test_nn_utils.py`.
Add grouped KV heads to your attention with an explicit map, query head \(h\) reads KV head \(\lfloor h/(H_q/H_{\mathrm{kv}}) \rfloor\), so that MHA and MQA are the two ends of one code path.
Write a slow reference that loops over heads with sliced weights, and compare outputs and gradients in `float64` with your batched path for MHA, GQA and MQA.
Assemble the decoder from one config object with optional embedding tying, and pass `test_transformer_block`, `test_transformer_lm` and `test_transformer_lm_truncated_input`.
Derive the parameter count of your config by hand and assert that it equals the count of unique registered parameters, tied and untied.

Write property tests showing RoPE preserves norms with scores depending only on relative position including offset equivalence, a future-token change leaves earlier outputs unchanged, and batch rows stay independent.
deliverables: The model package: components, config, grouped attention and the tied or untied head.
Your test suite: the head-loop oracle, float64 gradient comparisons, suffix-intervention tests and the parameter-count assertion.
A one-page shape and parameter sheet for your config, derived by hand.

checks.name: CS336 `tests/test_model.py` and the softmax test
checks.note: Use the untied head for the snapshot tests; test tying separately.

rubric.pass: All CS336 model tests and the softmax test pass.
rubric.strong: Your own tests add fully masked rows, padding plus causal masks and non-contiguous inputs.

rubric.pass: The batched attention matches the head loop on outputs.
rubric.strong: Outputs and all projection gradients match in `float64` for MHA, GQA and MQA within a stated tolerance.

rubric.pass: Changing a suffix leaves prefix logits unchanged.
rubric.strong: Your tests also show that the change does reach the logits at and after the edited position, and they cover batch independence.

rubric.pass: Your batched attention matches the head-loop reference for MHA, GQA and MQA, and the RoPE, causality and batch-independence tests pass.
rubric.strong: You explain why an interleaved KV expansion differs from the PyTorch grouping convention, and your weights load correctly under yours.

rubric.pass: The hand-derived parameter count equals the registered count.
rubric.strong: The sheet also gives the dominant forward FLOP terms and predicts how each scales when the sequence length doubles.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone artifact 2, the tiny decoder stack. Section 3 trains this model, and section 5 adds a cache to it.
